html:
The Golden Triangle is the hill region where Burma, Thailand and Laos meet, which from the 1950s became one of the world's main sources of opium and heroin. Most of the poppies grew in the Shan State of Burma.

Chinese Nationalist troops who fled into Shan State after 1949 organised the trade, and local warlords such as Khun Sa built armies on it. Drug money kept many of Burma's ethnic wars going.

From the 1990s methamphetamine pills joined heroin, flooding Asia. After the 2021 coup Burma again became the world's largest opium producer. Compare British opium in Bengal and heroin.
